text:
maria: Heads-up — p99 regression observed on streaming chat after the recent kernel selector change. Saw a 20-30% p99 increase on some workloads. Can we do a quick sync on mb-size heuristics vs non-streaming completions?

alex: Ack. Do you have a repro or traces yet?

maria: Minimal repro attached to the trace link: https://internal/traces/trace-2203456789 :eyes:
Key observations: streaming path with mbsize=4 shows higher tail than mbsize=1 in our canary GPU config. Non-streaming completions still prefer larger mbsize for throughput.

kevin: Interesting. That smells like KV-cache tail amplification when microbatches align poorly with streaming tail work. I saw similar in last quarter after the kernel map change.

sarah: Can you paste the perf counters / flamegraph snippet?

maria: Sure — quick perf dump from canary (filtered to request path):
```
config: mbsize=4, stream=true, kernel=auto-select-v2
p50: 28ms
p95: 120ms
p99: 420ms
kv-lookup-latency p99: 90ms
kernel-switch overhead p99: 60ms
per-request tailwork fraction: ~0.45
```
vs non-streaming with mbsize=8:
```
config: mbsize=8, stream=false, kernel=auto-select-v2
p50: 35ms
p95: 140ms
p99: 210ms
kv-lookup-latency p99: 40ms
kernel-switch overhead p99: 25ms
per-request tailwork fraction: ~0.12
```

alex: So streaming increases per-request tailwork (makes sense) and mbsize=4 seems to let more requests hit the tail concurrently, amplifying p99. Non-streaming batches absorb the cost.

kevin: Two hypotheses: (1) our kernel selector is choosing a kernel variant that has worse tail characteristics under intermittent KV misses; (2) batching heuristic doesn't distinguish streaming vs non-streaming latency SLOs.

maria: I instrumented the kernel decisions for the same trace: selector picked fast-path-fused kernel 72% of the time, fallback kernel for big sequences 28%. Fallbacks line up with KV misses + rare long prompts.

sarah: We should try: (A) bias selector away from the fallback kernel for streaming requests when SLOs prioritized; (B) reduce mbsize for streaming to 1 or 2 to lower amplification; (C) add a short idle-kv prefetch for streaming to reduce miss probability.

kevin: Agreed. Quick experiment plan: run 1) mbsize sweep [1,2,4] on streaming canary with current kernel selector, 2) same sweep with selector forced to conservative-kernel, 3) non-streaming sweep [4,8,16] for baseline. Capture p50/p95/p99 + kv-miss-rate.

maria: I'll spin up the sweep now and add traces to the shared folder. Starting run 1.

ci-bot: ci/canary-sweep #2203456789 started by maria — jobs: streaming-mb-1, streaming-mb-2, streaming-mb-4. Link: https://ci/internal/2203456789

alex: If sweep confirms, next steps: default heuristic: streaming -> prefer mbsize 1 or 2 and selector conservative; non-streaming -> keep larger mbsize for throughput. Also add metric alerts if streaming p99 grows >15% over baseline.

maria: Early numbers from run 1 (first 15m):
- mbsize=1 (streaming): p95 110ms, p99 160ms
- mbsize=2: p95 115ms, p99 240ms
- mbsize=4: p95 120ms, p99 420ms
kv-miss-rate roughly unchanged across mbsize (~4.3%)

kevin: That matches the amplification theory. Lower mbsize reduces contention at tail.

sarah: If kv-miss-rate unchanged, prefetch won't help much immediately. Kernel selector change + mbsize policy looks higher ROI.

maria: Filing a follow-up task: TG-4321 (streaming mbsize heuristic + kernel bias). I'll attach sweep artifacts and flamegraphs.

alex: Cool. Also let's document the regression root cause: kernel selector v2 becomes sensitive to interleaved KV misses in streaming, causing fallback kernel invocations that have higher tail cost. We'll need a regression note for the release.

maria: Noted. I'll draft the postmortem blurb and link TG-4321.

kevin: Thanks all — if nobody objects I'll start the conservative-kernel forced sweep after run 1 completes.

sarah: Go for it. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks team — updates in the TG and IFTT when canary finishes.
